[TUSTARI:79:40/r1] TUSTARI, d. 283 · author | holds | Only prophets and some, not all, of the truthful are free from appetite; freedom requires disciplining the self, and only prophets and some truthful people attain perfect discipline and character.
[TUSTARI:79:40/r2] TUSTARI, d. 283 · ابن السماك | reports | Ibn al-Sammak told his students that the cure they sought was to oppose their desires.
[TAB-FULL:v24p98#2/r1] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | holds | Al-Ṭabarī says the one who fears God, fulfills obligations, avoids sin, and restrains disliked desires has Paradise as the abode on Resurrection Day.
[NAHHAS:v5p146/r9] NAHHAS, d. 338 · author | holds | Fearing one's Lord's station means fearing account for sins; restraining the self means resisting desire for what is improper.
[SULAMI:v2p371#3/r1] SULAMI, d. 412 · بعضهم | reports | A person recognizes God's station through worldly signs and fears standing before Him at resurrection.
[SULAMI:v2p371#3/r2] SULAMI, d. 412 · ذو النون | reports | The fearful have ten stations: enduring sorrow, prevailing poverty, restless awe, abundant tears and supplication, flight from ease, bewilderment, a dissolved heart, troubled life, and concord with grief.
[SULAMI:v2p371#3/r3] SULAMI, d. 412 · بعضهم | reports | Real fear distracts a person from every comfort and holds him in grief until safety from fear appears.
[SULAMI:v2p371#3/r4] SULAMI, d. 412 · سهل | reports | Only prophets and some of the truthful are free from caprice; desire can still overpower reason and discernment through appetites.
[SULAMI:v2p371#3/r5] SULAMI, d. 412 · أبو بكر الوراق | reports | Nothing in either world is more vile than desire that opposes truth.
[SULAMI:v2p371#3/r6] SULAMI, d. 412 · الفضيل | reports | The best deeds oppose the lower self's desire.
[SULAMI:v2p371#3/r7] SULAMI, d. 412 · الجريري | reports | One who answers this divine address devotes a lifetime to struggle and enduring opposition to the self.
[SULAMI:v2p371#3/r8] SULAMI, d. 412 · الجنيد | reports | Junayd recounts meeting a stranger who had asked God to stir Junayd's heart; the stranger said the self's illness is cured by opposing its desire, a reply he had already heard seven times.
[MAWARDI-FULL:v6p199#2/r6] MAWARDI-FULL, d. 450 · مجاهد | reports | Fearing one's Lord's station means fearing God in this life when about to sin and then desisting.
[MAWARDI-FULL:v6p199#2/r7] MAWARDI-FULL, d. 450 · الربيع بن أنس | reports | It may mean fearing in the afterlife the standing before God for reckoning.
[MAWARDI-FULL:v6p199#2/r8] MAWARDI-FULL, d. 450 · الكلبي | reports | Restraining the self from desire means keeping it from sins and forbidden things.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p201/r1] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · author | holds | The explanation of fearing the Lord's standing is given earlier in Surat al-Rahman. | mentions 55:46
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p201/r2] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · عطاء والكلبي ومقاتل | reports | They report that the clause about restraining the self from desire was revealed concerning Musʿab ibn ʿUmayr.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p201/r3] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · author | holds | It means restraining oneself from desired forbidden acts and from desires formerly followed in the pre-Islamic period.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p201/r4] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · مقاتل | reports | A person may intend a sin, remember standing before God for reckoning, and then leave the sin; Paradise is that person's refuge and destination.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p201/r5] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · ابن عباس | reports | He says the refuge refers to Musʿab ibn ʿUmayr, about whom the verse was revealed, and then applies to anyone afterward with the same quality.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p201/r6] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · الفراء | reports | The refuge is for whoever has the described fear of the Lord and restrains the self from its desire.
[JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p262#2/r1] JURJANI-ASRAR, d. 471 · author | holds | A further kind of imaginative rhetoric makes the audience forget the simile and its figurative status; unlike the prior kind, that earlier example was explained by a rationale.
[JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p262#2/r2] JURJANI-ASRAR, d. 471 · author | holds | People figuratively described as rising in rank are made to seem physically high; Abū Tammām’s ignorant man imagines the climber needs something in the sky.
[JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p262#2/r3] JURJANI-ASRAR, d. 471 · author | holds | Ibn al-Rūmī depicts the Nūbakht family as learning astronomy by literally climbing toward the stars, not by calculation, then renews the claim with still greater force.
[JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p262#2/r4] JURJANI-ASRAR, d. 471 · author | holds | Calling a beautiful woman the sun and saying she shades someone from the sun suppresses awareness of metaphor; the wonder depends on asserting the paradox as literal fact.
[JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p262#2/r5] JURJANI-ASRAR, d. 471 · author | holds | Using a noun such as sun, moon, sea, or lion as if it named the target literally can make the wording seem to contain no simile or metaphor.
[DAMGHANI:v1p394/r7] DAMGHANI, d. 478 · author | holds | Maqām Rabbih means standing before God; fear of this standing is linked with Paradise and heed of God’s warning.
[DAMGHANI:v1p477/r13] DAMGHANI, d. 478 · author | holds | Hawā can mean desire or lust; Dāmghānī applies this sense to each of these passages and their parallels. | mentions 20:16, 28:50, 7:176, 25:43, 46:23
[JISHUMI:v10p7277/r1] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | holds | The verses distinguish obedience from rebellion: Paradise is attained through obedience and Hell deserved for sins, against the determinists' claim.
[JISHUMI:v10p7277/r3] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | holds | The Garden is earned by preferring obedience and avoiding sins; the command to restrain the self from desire includes both.
[JISHUMI:v10p7277/r6] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | holds | Obedience and sin are acts of human beings, as the verses attribute rebellion and fear to them; this refutes determinism.
[BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p330/r5] BAGHAWI-FULL, d. 516 · author | holds | Fearing the Lord’s standing means restraining oneself from forbidden desires; Muqatil describes someone recalling judgment while tempted and therefore refraining.
[KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p698#4/r1] KASHSHAF-FULL, d. 538 · author | holds | The soul is the self that commands evil; destructive desire means following appetites, which one must restrain and discipline through patience and preference for good.
[KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p698#4/r2] KASHSHAF-FULL, d. 538 · author | reports | One report says these verses were revealed about Abu Aziz ibn Umayr and Mus'ab ibn Umayr: Mus'ab killed his brother at Uhud and defended the Messenger until struck by arrows.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p435/r3] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | مقام ربه is the Resurrection and standing before God; attributing the station to God magnifies its terror and effect.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p435/r4] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn Abbas says the person fears God while committing a sin and therefore refrains from it.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p435/r5] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | الهوى means the soul's desires and similar inclinations, usually in a blameworthy sense.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p435/r6] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · سهل التستري | reports | Sahl al-Tustari says only prophets and some truthful saints escape desire.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p435/r7] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · بعض الحكماء | reports | Some sages advise opposing one's desire to reach what is correct.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p435/r8] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · الفضيل | reports | Al-Fudayl says the best deeds go against desire.
[TABRISI:79:45-46/r6] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | Fearing the Lord's station means fearing to be questioned for duties performed or omitted; restraining the soul means avoiding unlawful desires.
[TABRISI:79:45-46/r7] TABRISI, d. 548 · مقاتل | reports | A person may begin to intend a sin, then remember standing for judgment and abandon it.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p24#6/r1] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · author | holds | The explanation of fearing one's Lord's standing is given at al-Raḥmān 55:46. | mentions 55:46
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p24#7/r1] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · author | holds | One restrains the self from the forbidden things it desires.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p24#7/r2] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · مقاتل | reports | A person about to sin remembers standing before God for judgment and therefore abandons the sin.
[RAZI-FULL:v31p47#4/r1] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | Fear of one's Lord counters transgression, while restraining desire counters preferring worldly life; fear depends on knowledge (35:28) and causes restraint, so cause precedes effect. | mentions 79:17, 79:38, 35:28
[RAZI-FULL:v31p47#4/r2] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | The two descriptions encompass all virtues, just as the paired descriptions of Hell's people encompass all vices. | mentions 79:17, 79:38
[RAZI-FULL:v31p47#4/r3] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · قيل | reports | A reported occasion links the verses to Abu Aziz ibn Umayr and Musab ibn Umayr: Musab killed his brother at Uhud and shielded the Prophet until pierced by spears.
[QURTUBI-FULL:79:37-41/r10] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · مجاهد | reports | It is fearing God when about to sin in this life, then desisting. | mentions 55:46
[QURTUBI-FULL:79:37-41/r11] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | The verse forbids the self from sins and prohibited acts.
[QURTUBI-FULL:79:37-41/r12] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · سهل | reports | Abandoning desire is the key to Paradise, as this verse states.
[QURTUBI-FULL:79:37-41/r13] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · عبد الله بن مسعود | reports | People then lived when truth guided desire; a later age would have desire guiding truth, and he sought refuge from it.
[QURTUBI-FULL:79:37-41/r15] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · الضحاك عن ابن عباس | reports | The two verses concern Mus'ab ibn Umayr and his brother Amir: Amir was captured at Badr, identified himself as Mus'ab's brother, and was initially treated kindly until Mus'ab ordered the captors to bind him.
[QURTUBI-FULL:79:37-41/r16] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · الضحاك ع

ن ابن عباس | reports | Mus'ab said Amir was no brother to him and told the Ansar to bind their captive because their mother had wealth to ransom him.
[QURTUBI-FULL:79:37-41/r17] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · الضحاك عن ابن عباس | reports | Mus'ab was the one who feared his Lord's station: at Uhud he shielded the Prophet with his own body until arrows pierced him.
[QURTUBI-FULL:79:37-41/r7] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | Fearing one's Lord's station means fearing the moment of standing before Him.
[QURTUBI-FULL:79:37-41/r8] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · الربيع | reports | The feared station is the Day of Reckoning.
[QURTUBI-FULL:79:37-41/r9] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · قتادة | reports | Believers fear a station that belongs to God.
[QURTUBI-FULL:79:40/r1] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | reports | A report says Mus'ab killed his brother Amir at Badr.
[QURTUBI-FULL:79:40/r2] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · ابن عباس | reports | Another report says the verse concerned two men, Abu Jahl al-Makhzumi and Mus'ab al-Abdari.
[QURTUBI-FULL:79:40/r3] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · السدي | reports | He says the verse concerned Abu Bakr, who unknowingly ate food earned by his servant's fortune-telling, then vomited it after learning its source.
[QURTUBI-FULL:79:40/r4] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · السدي | reports | After vomiting, Abu Bakr prayed that any remaining food be held in his veins; the verse was then revealed.
[QURTUBI-FULL:79:40/r5] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · الكلبي وابن عباس | reports | The verse also describes someone able to commit a sin privately who refrains from fear of standing before God.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:79:37-40/r4] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | The person who fears standing before the Lord knows origin and return, and restrains desire because it leads to punishment.
[NASAFI-FULL:v4p316/r1] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | holds | Fearing one's Lord's standing means knowing that one will stand for judgment; the self is the commanding soul and desire is its harmful inclination.
[NASAFI-FULL:v4p316/r2] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | reports | Another view describes someone about to commit a sin who remembers the coming judgment and abandons it; desire is the soul's attraction to its cravings.
[QASHANI:79:34-41/r5] QASHANI, d. 736 · author | holds | The one fearing the Lord’s station ascends to heart and witnesses divine governance, restrains the self from desire through fear or awe, and reaches paradise according to rank.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p401/r3] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | Fear of the Lord's station means fear of standing before Him for judgment; the possessive phrase magnifies that awe.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p401/r4] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · ابن عباس | reports | He says the person feared God when he was about to sin and stopped himself.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p401/r5] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | Restraining the soul means restraining its desires, usually blameworthy; Sahl says only prophets and some truthful believers escape desire.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p401/r6] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · بعض الحكماء، عمران الميرتلي، الفضيل | reports | A wise saying advises opposing desire to reach right judgment; Imran's poem warns against obeying it; al-Fudayl calls resisting desire the best deed for both groups.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p317#2/r5] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · author | holds | Fearing one’s Lord means fearing to stand before Him and face His judgment, and restraining desire by returning oneself to obedience.
[BURHAN:v1p63/r8] BURHAN, d. 794 · author | rejects | The author suggests the singular “Paradise” in 79:41 may have driven al-Farrāʾ’s rhyme explanation, but the dual “both with branches” remains an objection to it. | mentions 79:40, 79:41, 20:117
[BURHAN:v2p296/r7] BURHAN, d. 794 · author | holds | Here desire stands for the sins the self desires; forbidding inclination itself is impossible, so the phrase means forbidding the self from following desire.
[BURHAN:v2p384/r1] BURHAN, d. 794 · جمهور الأمة | holds | The majority of the Muslim community holds that emphasis occurs in the Qur’an and Sunna.
[BURHAN:v2p384/r10] BURHAN, d. 794 · author | holds | Technical emphasis divides into verbal and semantic forms; verbal emphasis restates the first meaning with the same word or a synonym.
[BURHAN:v2p384/r2] BURHAN, d. 794 · قوم | reports | Some deny that emphasis exists in the Qur’an, Sunna, or language, insisting that each expression must add a new meaning.
[BURHAN:v2p384/r3] BURHAN, d. 794 · الملحدون | reports | Critics call emphasis pointless repetition and argue that eloquence requires concise wording; they suppose it reflects inability to express the intended meaning otherwise.
[BURHAN:v2p384/r4] BURHAN, d. 794 · الأصحاب | reports | The defenders answer that the Qur’an speaks in the Arabs’ language, where emphasis and repetition are recognized parts of eloquence and have many benefits.
[BURHAN:v2p384/r5] BURHAN, d. 794 · author | holds | The author says denial of emphasis in language is untenable: otherwise the term would have no known referent, and emphasis has many benefits.
[BURHAN:v2p384/r6] BURHAN, d. 794 · قوم | reports | Some classify emphasis as figurative because it contributes no meaning beyond the first expression; al-Tartusi records this position.
[BURHAN:v2p384/r7] BURHAN, d. 794 · author | prefers | The author holds emphasis to be literal: if the second identical ‘hurry’ were figurative, the first would be too, which is impossible because it precedes it.
[BURHAN:v2p384/r8] BURHAN, d. 794 · author | holds | Emphasis goes against the default reading, so a word should be parsed as emphatic only when an independent meaning cannot be assigned to it.
[BURHAN:v2p384/r9] BURHAN, d. 794 · author | rejects | The author rejects an unspecified criterion that accepts any meaning, since the meaning conveyed by a word is not itself another word-form that must imitate it.
[BIQAI-FULL:v8p308#s079/r1] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | The surah’s purpose is to establish resurrection and the gathering, displaying humanity’s final fate after the preceding surahs’ full exposition; its oaths show the matter has reached its decisive climax.
[BIQAI-FULL:v8p320/r4] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | Fear of standing before the Lord means fearing the encounter or its place and time, through awareness of His kindness and majesty; such fear presupposes belief in resurrection.
[BIQAI-FULL:v8p320/r5] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | The soul must be restrained from every desire, since the Fire is surrounded by appetites and religious law opposes what the lower self wants.
[BIQAI-FULL:v8p320/r6] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · الرازي | reports | Al-Rāzī defines blameworthy desire as appetite that conflicts with religious commands.
[BIQAI-FULL:v8p320/r7] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · الجنيد | reports | Al-Junayd says that when the self opposes its desire, its illness becomes its cure.
[BIQAI-FULL:v8p320/r8] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | The rhetorical arrangement uses transgression to imply the opposite of restraint and restraint to imply rejection of worldly preference.
[BURSEVI:v10p254#2/r1] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | Fearing the Lord’s station means fearing to stand before the Master for judgment on the great Day; such fear follows knowledge of creation and return.
[BURSEVI:v10p254#2/r2] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | reports | Maqam may be a verbal noun for standing, a place where servants stand for judgment and recompense, or an emphatic insertion.
[BURSEVI:v10p254#2/r3] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | Fear is paired with transgression because it is the first motive for obedience, followed by hope and then love; these suit ordinary people, the elect, and the most elect, respectively.
[BURSEVI:v10p254#2/r4] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | Restraining the self from desire means refusing natural appetites and worldly ornament because their consequences are harmful; hawa is desire without a religious warrant.
[BURSEVI:v10p254#2/r5] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · رسول الله | reports | The Prophet said his greatest fear for the community was desire and long hope: desire turns people from truth, while long hope makes them forget the afterlife.
[BURSEVI:v10p254#2/r6] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · بعض الكبار | reports | A great master says the seven desires listed in 3:14 reduce to worldly play and amusement, then to desire itself; escaping desire frees one from every bond and barrier. | mentions 3:14
[BURSEVI:v10p254#2/r7] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · سهل | reports | Sahl says only prophets and some, not all, of the truthful escape desire; one is safe by imposing proper discipline on oneself.
[BURSEVI:v10p254#2/r8] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | Bursevi describes the human as an isthmus between Divine and created, angelic and animal realities; from the higher aspect, a person restrains the lower self, as the Prophet addresses his human aspect from his angelic or unitive station.
[ALUSI-FULL:v30p36#4/r1] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | reports | مقام ربه may mean the servant's standing before his Lord on the Great Calamity and the day deeds are recalled, with the possessive construction compared to رقود حلب.
[ALUSI-FULL:v30p36#4/r2] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | reports | Alternatively the phrase means whoever fears his Lord, with مقام treated as extra; this rhetorically establishes fear of God, discussed at length in al-Rahman.
[ALUSI-FULL:v30p36#4/r3] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | Restrain the self from destructive desire by patience, preferring good works, and refusing to be deceived by worldly pleasure and ornament.
[ALUSI-FULL:v30p36#4/r4] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · ابن عباس ومقاتل | reports | Ibn Abbas and Muqatil describe a person who considers a sin, recalls standing before God in judgment, fears that meeting, and abandons the sin.
[ALUSI-FULL:v30p36#4/r5] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · الراغب | reports | Al-Raghib explains the name هوا by the way desire carries its follower toward weakness in this world and the abyss in the next.

] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · بعض الحكماء | reports | A maxim says that one finds the right answer by looking at one's desire and opposing it; al-Fudayl calls opposition to desire the best deed.
[ALUSI-FULL:v30p36#4/r7] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · أبو عمران الميرتلي | reports | Abu Imran al-Mirtalli's poem warns that obeying desire or a stubborn self leads a person to ruin.
[ALUSI-FULL:v30p36#5/r2] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn Abbas says the two verses concern the brothers Abu ʿAziz and Musʿab: one was tyrannical and worldly, while Musʿab feared God and restrained desire.
[ALUSI-FULL:v30p36#5/r3] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | reports | Musʿab protected the Prophet at Uhud and died pierced by arrows; the Prophet said he entrusted him to God and recalled his two cloaks and golden sandal strap.
[ALUSI-FULL:v30p36#5/r4] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · الكشاف | reports | Al-Kashshaf says Musʿab killed his captured brother Abu ʿAziz at Uhud; the account says their mother was exceptionally wealthy.
[ALUSI-FULL:v30p36#5/r5] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · ابن عباس | reports | Another report from Ibn Abbas connects the two verses to Abu Jahl and Musʿab; another says the first verse concerned al-Nadr and his son al-Harith.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p88/r4] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | The warning and glad tidings follow the proof of resurrection because judgment follows resurrection; the wise prepare for lasting reward rather than transient pleasure.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p92/r2] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | The blame concerns choosing worldly life over the afterlife; worldly benefits that do not cost one the afterlife are not blameworthy, as the counsel to Qarun shows. | mentions 28:77
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p92/r3] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | The two clauses are parallel: fearing the Lord counters transgression, while restraining the self from desire counters preferring worldly life.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p92/r4] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | Restraining one's self personifies it as another who urges sin; this rhetorical self-separation is illustrated by Urwa ibn Udhayna's verse about heart and conscience.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p92/r5] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · عروة بن أذينة | reports | His verse illustrates the inner dialogue by which the heart appeals to conscience to restrain the self's impulses.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p92/r6] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | Hawa means what the soul desires, especially appetites or anger contrary to truth and complete benefit; since such desire is unguided, ‘without guidance’ in 28:50 is emphatic. | mentions 28:50
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p92/r7] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | The generic definite article in al-hawa denotes the class of desire.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p93/r2] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | ‘The station of his Lord’ figuratively conveys divine majesty and awe, naming the place of standing for what is associated with it. | mentions 14:14, 55:46
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p93/r3] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | The paired descriptions of remembering and the Garden use a collect-then-divide rhetorical structure; ‘the self’ has the same generic definite sense as ‘the abode.’
[TABATABAI:79:1-41#3/r1] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · author | holds | God's station as Lord includes the attributes entailed by lordship, such as knowledge, absolute power, dominance, mercy, and wrath; it is the source of forgiveness for believers and punishment for deniers. | mentions 20:81, 20:82, 15:49, 15:50
[TABATABAI:79:1-41#4/r1] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · author | holds | The station feared is God's lordship, the source of mercy for faithful people and painful punishment for those who deny and disobey.
[TABATABAI:79:1-41#4/r12] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · جعفر الصادق | reports | Al-Sadiq says that knowing God sees, hears, and knows one's deeds restrains a person from wrongdoing; the author says this supports his interpretation of fearing God's station.
[TABATABAI:79:1-41#4/r13] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · علي | reports | Ali warns that following desire turns people away from truth, while long hopes make them forget the afterlife.
[TABATABAI:79:1-41#4/r2] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · قيل | rejects | One view says it is the servant's standing before God on Judgment Day to answer for deeds; the author dismisses this reading.
